chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Temporary marriage (al-Mut'ah) is that upon which the Quran was revealed and the Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was established."

key_terms.الْمُتْعَةُ: Temporary marriage (Mut'ah), a specific type of marriage contract with a fixed duration and dowry.
key_terms.نَزَلَ بِهَا: Revealed regarding it, indicating Quranic basis.

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic and Prophetic basis for temporary marriage (Mut'ah) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes Mut'ah as a practice rooted in both Quranic revelation and continuous Prophetic Sunnah, affirming its status as a distinct marital contract in Shia jurisprudence. Scholars emphasize the phrase 'nuzila biha al-Qur'an' to argue that the permissibility was explicitly revealed, distinguishing it from abrogated verses. This narration serves as a foundational proof for the permanence of Mut'ah until the Day of Resurrection, countering Sunni claims of abrogation.
